claim: SOX2 expression levels are crucial for the balance between maintenance and differentiation of airway progenitor cells during development and regeneration.
source: SOX2 expression levels are crucial for the balance between maintenance and differentiation of airway progenitor cells during development and regeneration.
evidence: This is a central claim stated in the abstract, supported by the experimental data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: SOX21 coincides with high levels of SOX2 during development in the mouse proximal airway epithelium.
source: Here, we describe patterning of the mouse proximal airway epithelium by SOX21, which coincides with high levels of SOX2 during development.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Airway progenitor cells in the SOX2+/SOX21+ zone show differentiation to basal cells, specifying cells for the extrapulmonary airways.
source: Airway progenitor cells in this SOX2+/SOX21+ zone show differentiation to basal cells, specifying cells for the extrapulmonary airways.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2 showing TRP63+ basal cells in the SOX2+/SOX21+ zone.

claim: Loss of SOX21 showed an increased differentiation of SOX2+ progenitor cells to basal and ciliated cells during mouse lung development.
source: Loss of SOX21 showed an increased differentiation of SOX2+ progenitor cells to basal and ciliated cells during mouse lung development.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative data from Sox21+/− and Sox21−/− mice shown in Figure 3.

claim: SOX21 inhibits differentiation of airway progenitors by antagonizing SOX2-induced expression of specific genes involved in airway differentiation.
source: We propose a mechanism where SOX21 inhibits differentiation of airway progenitors by antagonizing SOX2-induced expression of specific genes involved in airway differentiation.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by luciferase assay data in Figure 3F showing SOX21 suppression of SOX2-activated promoters.

claim: In the adult tracheal epithelium, SOX21 inhibits basal to ciliated cell differentiation.
source: Additionally, in the adult tracheal epithelium, SOX21 inhibits basal to ciliated cell differentiation.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by ALI culture data from Sox21+/− mice shown in Figure 4.

claim: SOX2 mainly drives differentiation of epithelial cells during development and regeneration after injury.
source: This suppressing function of SOX21 on differentiation contrasts SOX2, which mainly drives differentiation of epithelial cells during development and regeneration after injury.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by data from Sox2+/− mice and naphthalene injury experiments shown in Figures 3 and 5.

claim: SOX2+/SOX21+ regionalization is conserved in human fetal lung organoids and adult bronchial epithelial cells.
source: Furthermore, using human fetal lung organoids and adult bronchial epithelial cells, we show that SOX2+/SOX21+ regionalization is conserved.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by immunofluorescence data from human samples shown in Figures 6 and 7.

claim: The interplay between SOX2 and SOX21 is context and concentration dependent leading to regulation of differentiation of the airway epithelium.
source: Lastly, we show that the interplay between SOX2 and SOX21 is context and concentration dependent leading to regulation of differentiation of the airway epithelium.
evidence: This claim is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experimental approaches including dose-dependent luciferase assays and heterozygous mouse models.

claim: The earliest expression of SOX21 during lung development was found at gestational age E11.5.
source: The earliest expression of SOX21 during lung development was found at gestational age E11.5.
evidence: This claim is directly stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1A.

claim: SOX2 expression can be detected at E9.5, therefore SOX2 expression precedes SOX21.
source: SOX2 expression, which can be detected at E9.5, therefore precedes SOX21 (Que et al., 2007; Gontan et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: At E11.5, abundant SOX21 expression was seen in cells of the thymus and esophagus, which also co-expressed SOX2.
source: At E11.5, abundant SOX21 expression was seen in cells of the thymus and esophagus, which also co-expressed SOX2.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1A.

claim: From E13.5 onwards, SOX21 was expressed throughout the trachea and main bronchi, but was absent in the smaller SOX2+ airways.
source: From E13.5 onwards, SOX21 was expressed throughout the trachea and main bronchi, but was absent in the smaller SOX2+ airways.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1A.

claim: Four zones can be distinguished in the developing lung epithelium from proximal to distal: zone 1 (SOX2+SOX21+), zone 2 (SOX2+ only), zone 3 (transition zone with SOX9+ to SOX2+), and zone 4 (SOX9+ distal progenitors).
source: Labeling from proximal to distal, four zones could be distinguished in the developing lung epithelium (Figure 1A): zone 1, the most proximal zone, comprised the developing trachea and main bronchi, which contain SOX2+SOX21+ airway epithelial cells; zone 2, which contains only SOX2+ airway epithelial cells; zone 3, a transition zone, in which distal SOX9+ progenitors transition into SOX2+ airway progenitors (Mahoney et al., 2014); and zone 4, the most distal part of the lung epithelium containing SOX9+ progenitors (Rawlins et al., 2009a; Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data and schematic diagrams in Figure 1A.

claim: SOX21 was never observed in the distal buds, but always in cells that also express SOX2.
source: SOX21 was never observed in the distal buds, but always in cells that also express SOX2.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1A.

claim: SOX21 shows different expression levels among cells during the early developmental stages (E12.5–E14.5), in stark contrast to the more homogeneous distribution of SOX2.
source: SOX21 shows different expression levels among cells during the early developmental stages (E12.5–E14.5), in stark contrast to the more homogeneous distribution of SOX2 (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1A.

claim: At E18.5, SOX21 is homogeneously expressed in the trachea, heterogeneously expressed in the main bronchi and absent in the intrapulmonary airways.
source: At E18.5, SOX21 is homogeneously expressed in the trachea, heterogeneously expressed in the main bronchi and absent in the intrapulmonary airways (Figure 1A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1A.

claim: SOX21 is expressed specifically in the extrapulmonary airways (trachea and main bronchi) during the formation of the airway tree, which is the most proximal part of the SOX2+ epithelium.
source: In summary, SOX21 is expressed specifically in the extrapulmonary airways (trachea and main bronchi) during the formation of the airway tree, which is the most proximal part of the SOX2+ epithelium.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Results section supported by the immunofluorescence data presented in Figure 1.

claim: SOX21 has a unilateral expression pattern in the main bronchi, starting from the bifurcation of the trachea (the carina).
source: We also observed a unilateral expression of SOX21 in the main bronchi, starting from the bifurcation of the trachea (the carina) (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1A and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: SOX21 is abundantly expressed on the medial side of the airway, but almost completely absent on the lateral side.
source: SOX21 is abundantly expressed on the medial side of the airway, but almost completely absent on the lateral side (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The unilateral expression pattern of SOX21 is present during branching morphogenesis but becomes less apparent after E15.5.
source: This unilateral expression pattern is present during branching morphogenesis but becomes less apparent after E15.5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A.

claim: SOX2 was found to be higher expressed in the dorsal compared to the ventral side of the tracheal epithelium during development.
source: Previously, SOX2 was found to be higher expressed in the dorsal compared to the ventral side of the tracheal epithelium (TE) during development (Que et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In the developing trachea, the ventral side is marked by SOX9+ cartilage nodules and the dorsal side by smooth muscle actin+ (SMA+) mesenchymal cells.
source: In the developing trachea, the ventral side is marked by SOX9+ cartilage nodules and the dorsal side by smooth muscle actin+ (SMA+) mesenchymal cells (Hines et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SOX21 is more abundantly expressed on the dorsal side of the trachea, comparable to the location of high SOX2 levels.
source: We therefore made transverse sections from the trachea up to the main bronchi and observed a more abundant expression of SOX21 on the dorsal side, comparable to the location of high SOX2 levels (Figure 1B).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1B.

claim: High expression of SOX2 is important to set up the expression pattern of SOX21 during lung development.
source: We hypothesize that the high expression of SOX2 is important to set up the expression pattern of SOX21 during lung development.
evidence: This is a hypothesis stated in the Results section, supported by the correlation between high SOX2 and SOX21 expression patterns.

claim: Both MYC-SOX2 and MYC-SOX21 expression caused the appearance of cystic structures in the lung.
source: Both MYC-SOX2 and MYC-SOX21 expression caused the appearance of cystic structures, albeit much smaller in the MYC-SOX21 model (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by bright field images in Figure 1—figure supplement 1C.

claim: MYC-SOX2-expressing cells in the distal lung buds lost SOX9 while inducing Sox21.
source: Although a similar phenotype was observed, MYC-SOX2-expressing cells in the distal lung buds lost SOX9 while inducing Sox21, but MYC-SOX21-expressing cells in the distal bud retained SOX9+ and did not induce Sox2 expression.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1C.

claim: MYC-SOX21-expressing cells in the distal bud retained SOX9+ and did not induce Sox2 expression.
source: Although a similar phenotype was observed, MYC-SOX2-expressing cells in the distal lung buds lost SOX9 while inducing Sox21, but MYC-SOX21-expressing cells in the distal bud retained SOX9+ and did not induce Sox2 expression.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 1C.

claim: SOX2 alone can set up Sox21 expression.
source: We therefore conclude that SOX2 alone can set up Sox21 expression, but SOX21 alone is not sufficient to induce a SOX2+ airway cell fate in the in the presence of distal mesenchymal signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the transgenic mouse experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: SOX21 alone is not sufficient to induce a SOX2+ airway cell fate in the presence of distal mesenchymal signaling.
source: We therefore conclude that SOX2 alone can set up Sox21 expression, but SOX21 alone is not sufficient to induce a SOX2+ airway cell fate in the in the presence of distal mesenchymal signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the transgenic mouse experiments shown in Figure 1C.

claim: At E11.5, the esophagus and thymus already contained TRP63+ epithelial cell progenitors.
source: At this embryonic age, the esophagus and thymus already contained TRP63+ epithelial cell progenitors (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), while TRP63+ basal cells only start to appear in the lung at E12.5 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: TRP63+ basal cells only start to appear in the lung at E12.5.
source: At this embryonic age, the esophagus and thymus already contained TRP63+ epithelial cell progenitors (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A), while TRP63+ basal cells only start to appear in the lung at E12.5 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2A.

claim: SOX2 directly regulates Trp63 expression.
source: Previously, we showed that SOX2 directly regulates Trp63 expression (Ochieng et al., 2014), and we therefore analyzed whether SOX21 plays a role in the differentiation of airway progenitor cells to basal cells.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous work by the authors.

claim: TRP63+ basal cells appear in zone 1 from E12.5 onward, but not in zone 2.
source: We found that TRP63+ basal cells appear in zone 1 from E12.5 onward, but not in zone 2 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2A.

claim: At E14.5, higher expression of SOX2 and SOX21 as well as more basal cells were found in the epithelium in close proximity to SMA+ mesenchymal cells.
source: At E14.5, we found higher expression of SOX2 and SOX21 as well as more basal cells in the epithelium in close proximity to SMA+ mesenchymal cells (Figure 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figures 1 and 2—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: The specific localization of basal cells is consistent with previous findings.
source: This localization of basal cells is consistent with previous findings (Que et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Mesenchymal–epithelial crosstalk is involved in the combined SOX21 and SOX2 expression and in the progenitor to basal cell differentiation.
source: The specific localization suggests that mesenchymal–epithelial crosstalk is involved in the combined SOX21 and SOX2 expression and in the progenitor to basal cell differentiation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the spatial correlation between mesenchymal markers and SOX2/SOX21 expression.

claim: Within the extended SOX2+SOX21+ zone 1 in iSox2SPC-rtTA and iSox21SPC-rtTA mice, TPR63+ basal cells were present.
source: Within the extended SOX2+SOX21+ zone 1, TPR63+ basal cells were also present, showing that induction of both SOX2 and SOX21 is sufficient for the differentiation of airway progenitors to TPR63+ basal cells and can be independent on anatomical localization (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Induction of both SOX2 and SOX21 is sufficient for the differentiation of airway progenitors to TPR63+ basal cells and can be independent on anatomical localization.
source: Within the extended SOX2+SOX21+ zone 1, TPR63+ basal cells were also present, showing that induction of both SOX2 and SOX21 is sufficient for the differentiation of airway progenitors to TPR63+ basal cells and can be independent on anatomical localization (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the transgenic mouse experiments shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: Conditional deletion of β-catenin in SPC+ cells during lung development caused the appearance of cystic structures and an increased number of TRP63+ basal cells.
source: Previously, conditional deletion of β-catenin in SPC+ cells during lung development caused the appearance of cystic structures, just like after SOX2 and SOX21 induction. Upon β-catenin deletion, an increased number of TRP63+ basal cells was found, of which a subset co-expressed SOX9 (Ustiyan et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: SOX9+ basal cells were found in the iSox2SPC-rtTA and iSox21SPC-rtTA mouse lungs, while only sporadic SOX9+ basal cells were detected in the control.
source: Similarly, we found SOX9+ basal cells in the iSox2SPC-rtTA and iSox21SPC-rtTA mouse lungs, while only sporadic SOX9+ basal cells were detected in the control (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: In both iSox2CC10-rtTA and iSox21CC10-rtTA models, there was a decreased number of secretory cells.
source: In both models, we found a decreased number of secretory cells (Figure 2C), a slight decrease of total number of ciliated cells (Figure 2D, grey bar) and an increase in the total number of basal cells (Figure 2E, grey bar).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 2C.

claim: In both iSox2CC10-rtTA and iSox21CC10-rtTA models, there was a slight decrease of total number of ciliated cells.
source: In both models, we found a decreased number of secretory cells (Figure 2C), a slight decrease of total number of ciliated cells (Figure 2D, grey bar) and an increase in the total number of basal cells (Figure 2E, grey bar).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 2D.

claim: In both iSox2CC10-rtTA and iSox21CC10-rtTA models, there was an increase in the total number of basal cells.
source: In both models, we found a decreased number of secretory cells (Figure 2C), a slight decrease of total number of ciliated cells (Figure 2D, grey bar) and an increase in the total number of basal cells (Figure 2E, grey bar).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 2E.

claim: TRP63+ basal cell numbers increased mostly on the lateral side of the airway in iSox2CC10-rtTA and iSox21CC10-rtTA models.
source: Reminiscent of the unilateral expression of SOX21 during development, TRP63+ basal cell numbers increased mostly on the lateral side of the airway, while a decrease in secretory cells was observed on both sides.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 2E.

claim: A difference in medial and lateral mesenchymal-epithelial signaling directs the induced differentiation of MYC-SOX2 or MYC-SOX21 expressing cells.
source: This suggests that a difference in medial and lateral mesenchymal-epithelial signaling directs the induced differentiation of MYC-SOX2 or MYC-SOX21 expressing cells.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the unilateral increase in basal cells.

claim: MYC expressing cells in iSox2CC10-rtTA and iSox21CC10-rtTA models were mostly negative for basal cell marker TRP63, secretory cell marker SCGB1A1, and ciliated cell marker FOXJ1.
source: Focusing on the MYC expressing cells, we observed that these cells were mostly negative for basal cell marker TRP63, secretory cell marker SCGB1A1, and ciliated cell marker FOXJ1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Upon the induction of MYC-SOX2 or MYC-SOX21, the secretory cell identity is rapidly lost as shown by the loss of SCGB1A1 expression.
source: This suggests that upon the induction of MYC-SOX2 or MYC-SOX21, the secretory cell identity is rapidly lost as shown by the loss of SCGB1A1 expression.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the immunofluorescence data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Upon loss of SCGB1A1 expression, the SCGB1A1/CC10-driven MYC transgene is no longer expressed and cells adopt a TRP63+ basal cell fate.
source: Concomitantly, the SCGB1A1/CC10-driven MYC transgene is no longer expressed and cells adopt a TRP63+ basal cell fate (Figure 2F).
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the immunofluorescence data in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Sox21−/− mice do not show respiratory distress at birth.
source: Sox21−/− mice do not show respiratory distress at birth (Kiso et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Sox21−/− mouse lungs are smaller compared to wild-type littermate controls but have no apparent branching defect.
source: Their lungs are smaller compared to wild-type littermate controls but have no apparent branching defect (data not shown).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section but the supporting data is not shown in the manuscript.

claim: At E14.5, there was an increased number of basal cells in Sox21+/− mice, which was even more pronounced in Sox21−/− mice.
source: At E14.5, we found an increased number of basal cells in Sox21+/− mice, which was even more pronounced in Sox21-/- mice (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 3A.

claim: A decrease in the number of basal cells is observed in lungs of Sox2+/− at E14.5.
source: In contrast, a decrease in the number of basal cells is observed in lungs of Sox2+/− at E14.5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A), corresponding with the dose-dependent role described for SOX2 in airway differentiation (Que et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Reduced levels of SOX2 and SOX21 appear to oppositely affect airway progenitor cell differentiation.
source: Hence, reduced levels of SOX2 and SOX21 appear to oppositely affect airway progenitor cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the comparison of Sox2+/− and Sox21+/− mice.

claim: SOX21 maintains the SOX2 progenitor state, while SOX2 expression is needed to initiate progenitor to basal cell differentiation.
source: SOX21 maintains the SOX2 progenitor state, while SOX2 expression is needed to initiate progenitor to basal cell differentiation.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the comparison of Sox2+/− and Sox21+/− mice.

claim: At E14.5, there was a small increase of TRP73+- and FOXJ1+-ciliated cells in Sox21+/− airways and an even larger increase in Sox21−/− airways.
source: At E14.5, there was a small increase of TRP73+- and FOXJ1+-ciliated cells in Sox21+/− airways and an even larger increase in Sox21−/− airways (Figure 3B,C), reaffirming that SOX21 levels are important for maintenance of the progenitor state and suppression of differentiation.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 3B,C.

claim: In the Sox2+/− mice, TRP73+- and FOXJ1+-ciliated cell numbers did not differ from wild-type controls.
source: In the Sox2+/− mice, TRP73+- and FOXJ1+-ciliated cell numbers did not differ from wild-type controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C), suggesting that decreasing SOX2 levels do not influence the initiation of ciliated cell differentiation.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Decreasing SOX2 levels do not influence the initiation of ciliated cell differentiation.
source: In the Sox2+/− mice, TRP73+- and FOXJ1+-ciliated cell numbers did not differ from wild-type controls (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B,C), suggesting that decreasing SOX2 levels do not influence the initiation of ciliated cell differentiation.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the data from Sox2+/− mice.

claim: Overall proliferation was unaltered during development in Sox2+/− airways and only slightly increased in Sox21−/− airways.
source: Moreover, overall proliferation was unaltered during development in Sox2+/− airways and only slightly increased in Sox21−/− airways (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that SOX2 and SOX21 act mainly on differentiation and not proliferation.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 3D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1D.

claim: SOX2 and SOX21 act mainly on differentiation and not proliferation.
source: Moreover, overall proliferation was unaltered during development in Sox2+/− airways and only slightly increased in Sox21−/− airways (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 1D), suggesting that SOX2 and SOX21 act mainly on differentiation and not proliferation.
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the proliferation data from Sox2+/− and Sox21−/− mice.

claim: At E18.5, the increase in basal cell numbers in Sox21−/− observed at E14.5 was no longer detectable.
source: At E18.5, the increase in basal cell numbers in Sox21−/− observed at E14.5 was no longer detectable, although increased numbers of ciliated cells were still present.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 3E.

claim: At E18.5, increased numbers of ciliated cells were still present in Sox21−/− mice.
source: At E18.5, the increase in basal cell numbers in Sox21−/− observed at E14.5 was no longer detectable, although increased numbers of ciliated cells were still present.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 3E.

claim: At E18.5, there was a decrease in secretory cells in Sox21−/− mice.
source: Additionally, we also observed a decrease in secretory cells at E18.5 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 3E.

claim: In the absence of SOX21, the increase in ciliated cells is at the expense of secretory cells.
source: Thus, it seems that in the absence of SOX21 the increase in ciliated cells is at the expense of secretory cells, in agreement with the reported finding that the secretory cell lineage gives rise to ciliated cells (Rawlins et al., 2009b).
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the data from Sox21−/− mice and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: In Sox2+/− lungs, only a minor decrease in secretory cells was observed at E18.5.
source: In Sox2+/− lungs, only a minor decrease in secretory cells was observed at E18.5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1E.

claim: SOX2 activates its own promoter, as well as the promoter regions of the Trp63 and Trp73 genes.
source: We found that SOX2 activates its own promoter, as well as the promoter regions of the Trp63 and Trp73 genes (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by luciferase assay data in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: Putative binding sites for SOX21 were identified in the promoter regions of Sox2, Trp63, and Trp73.
source: SOX21 binding motifs have been characterized through chromatin immunoprecipitation (Matsuda et al., 2012), and we subsequently identified putative binding sites for SOX21 in the promoter regions of Sox2, Trp63, and Trp73 (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by in silico analysis and luciferase assay data in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: When increasing amounts of SOX21 were titrated in with SOX2, luciferase activity with the Trp63 promotor significantly decreased.
source: When increasing amounts of SOX21 were titrated in with SOX2, luciferase activity with the Trp63 promotor significantly decreased (Figure 3F, Figure 3—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by luciferase assay data in Figure 3F and Figure 3—figure supplement 1F.

claim: SOX21 can suppress promotor regions of SOX2 target genes.
source: This shows that SOX21 can suppress promotor regions of SOX2 target genes.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the luciferase assay data.

claim: High levels of SOX2 initiate SOX21 expression, marking a zone of the proximal airways where progenitor cells start to differentiate.
source: Taken together, we propose that high levels of SOX2 initiate SOX21 expression, marking a zone of the proximal airways where progenitor cells start to differentiate.
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the Results section based on the collective data from the experiments.

claim: Within the zone where progenitor cells start to differentiate, SOX21 and SOX2 in progenitor cells have a regulatory function, by maintaining a balance between progenitor maintenance and differentiation.
source: Within this zone, SOX21 and SOX2 in progenitor cells have a regulatory function, by maintaining a balance between progenitor maintenance and differentiation (Figure 3G).
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the Results section based on the collective data from the experiments.

claim: At E18.5, SOX2 and SOX21 remain expressed in the extrapulmonary airways, the region where basal cells are maintained.
source: At E18.5, SOX2 and SOX21 remain expressed in the extrapulmonary airways, the region where basal cells are maintained.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data.

claim: Basal cells are important for regeneration after injury, as they can proliferate and differentiate to secretory and ciliated cells.
source: Basal cells are important for regeneration after injury, as they can proliferate and differentiate to secretory and ciliated cells (Rock et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Sox2 and Sox21 were both expressed at baseline levels at the start of ALI and their levels gradually increased in the initial days of ALI differentiation.
source: Using this model, we show that Sox2 and Sox21 were both expressed at baseline levels at the start of ALI and that their levels gradually increased in the initial days of ALI differentiation (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by qPCR data in Figure 4A.

claim: SOX2 and SOX21 are expressed in basal and apical cells on ALI day 10, although both proteins were heterogeneously distributed among the two cell layers.
source: Immunofluorescence analysis on ALI day 10 showed expression of SOX2 and SOX21 in basal and apical cells, although both proteins were heterogeneously distributed among the two cell layers (Figure 4B).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 4B.

claim: Cells highly expressing SOX2 were frequently high in SOX21 expression and vice versa.
source: Cells highly expressing SOX2 were frequently high in SOX21 expression and vice versa (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by fluorescence intensity measurements in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Basal cells were mainly Sox2lowSox21low (80.5%).
source: Basal cells were mainly Sox2lowSox21low (80.5%), while ciliated cells were either SOX2highSOX21high (77.7%) or SOX2highSOX21low (14.5%; Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by fluorescence intensity measurements in Figure 4C.

claim: Ciliated cells were either SOX2highSOX21high (77.7%) or SOX2highSOX21low (14.5%).
source: Basal cells were mainly Sox2lowSox21low (80.5%), while ciliated cells were either SOX2highSOX21high (77.7%) or SOX2highSOX21low (14.5%; Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by fluorescence intensity measurements in Figure 4C.

claim: In the adult mouse TE, SOX2 and SOX21 levels were similar between cell types in vivo.
source: In the adult mouse TE, SOX2 and SOX21 levels were similar between cell types in vivo (Figure 5A), suggesting that these are stable for the maintenance of TE and only increase when differentiation is initiated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5A.

claim: SOX2 and SOX21 levels are stable for the maintenance of TE and only increase when differentiation is initiated.
source: In the adult mouse TE, SOX2 and SOX21 levels were similar between cell types in vivo (Figure 5A), suggesting that these are stable for the maintenance of TE and only increase when differentiation is initiated (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the comparison of in vivo and in vitro data.

claim: In Sox21+/− ALI cultures, more basal cells differentiated to FOXJ1+ ciliated cells compared to WT.
source: In Sox21+/− ALI cultures, more basal cells differentiated to FOXJ1+ ciliated cells compared to WT (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 4D.

claim: In Sox2+/− ALI cultures, fewer basal cells differentiated to ciliated cells compared to WT, as shown by a significant decrease of both single TRP73+ and FOXJ1+ cells.
source: In Sox2+/− ALI cultures, fewer basal cells differentiated to ciliated cells compared to WT, as was shown by a significant decrease of both single TRP73+ and FOXJ1+ cells (Figure 4D; Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 4D and Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claim: The differentiation capacity towards secretory cells was not affected in either Sox2+/− or Sox21+/− ALI cultures compared to WT.
source: The differentiation capacity towards secretory cells was not affected in either Sox2+/− or Sox21+/− ALI cultures compared to WT (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 4D.

claim: SOX2 and SOX21 levels are mainly involved in balancing the differentiation of basal cells to ciliated cells, with SOX2 stimulating differentiation and SOX21 inhibiting differentiation.
source: Therefore, SOX2 and SOX21 levels are mainly involved in balancing the differentiation of basal cells to ciliated cells, with SOX2 stimulating differentiation and SOX21 inhibiting differentiation (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the ALI culture data from Sox2+/− and Sox21+/− mice.

claim: Induction of either MYC-SOX2 or MYC-SOX21 in adult mice resulted in a decrease in secretory cells.
source: Induction of either MYC-SOX2 or MYC-SOX21 resulted in a decrease in secretory cells, while MYC-SOX2 also increased TRP63+ basal cell numbers (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 4E.

claim: MYC-SOX2 induction in adult mice increased TRP63+ basal cell numbers.
source: Induction of either MYC-SOX2 or MYC-SOX21 resulted in a decrease in secretory cells, while MYC-SOX2 also increased TRP63+ basal cell numbers (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 4E.

claim: MYC-SOX2 induction in secretory cells drives the appearance of basal cells.
source: Thus, MYC-SOX2 induction in secretory cells drives the appearance of basal cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the data from iSox2CC10-rtTA adult mice.

claim: The induction of MYC-SOX21 in secretory cells of adult airway epithelium resulted in a loss of secretory phenotype but appears insufficient to drive differentiation toward a basal or ciliated cell type.
source: In addition, the induction of MYC-SOX21 in secretory cells of adult airway epithelium resulted in a loss of secretory phenotype but appears insufficient to drive differentiation toward a basal or ciliated cell type (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the data from iSox21CC10-rtTA adult mice.

claim: SOX21 remains expressed throughout the tracheal epithelium (TE) in both basal and non-basal cells in adult mice.
source: SOX21 remains expressed throughout the tracheal epithelium (TE) in both basal and non-basal cells in adult mice (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5A.

claim: SOX21-expressing cells were observed in the submucosal glands (SMG), which also contribute to TE regeneration after injury.
source: In addition, we observed SOX21-expressing cells in the submucosal glands (SMG), which also contribute to TE regeneration after injury (Lynch et al., 2018; Tata et al., 2018; Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5A and citations to previous literature.

claim: SOX9+ SMG cells surface at the TE after administering a high naphthalene dose and thereby contribute to repair of the TE.
source: SOX9+ SMG cells surface at the TE after administering a high naphthalene dose and thereby contribute to repair of the TE (Lynch et al., 2018; Tata et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SOX2 or SOX21 expression was unaltered at 2 DPI compared to CO exposed mice.
source: However, we found that SOX2 or SOX21 expression was unaltered at 2 DPI compared to CO exposed mice, suggesting that SOX2 downregulation at 1 DPI is temporary and a consequence of naphthalene administration (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1B.

claim: SOX2 downregulation at 1 DPI is temporary and a consequence of naphthalene administration.
source: However, we found that SOX2 or SOX21 expression was unaltered at 2 DPI compared to CO exposed mice, suggesting that SOX2 downregulation at 1 DPI is temporary and a consequence of naphthalene administration (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an inference stated in the Results section based on the comparison of expression at different time points after injury.

claim: After 5 days, there was a decrease of SOX9+ cells in Sox2+/− TE, and a small increase of SOX9+ cells in Sox21+/− TE compared to WT and to each other.
source: After 5 days, we observed a decrease of SOX9+ cells in Sox2+/− TE, and a small increase of SOX9+ cells in Sox21+/− TE compared to WT and to each other (Figure 5C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 5C.

claim: SOX2 and SOX21 levels are important for TE regeneration by SOX9+ SMG cells.
source: This shows that SOX2 and SOX21 levels are important for TE regeneration by SOX9+ SMG cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the data from Sox2+/− and Sox21+/− mice after naphthalene injury.

claim: At 20 DPI, fewer FOXJ1+ ciliated cells, but more dividing and non-dividing basal cells were observed in Sox2+/− TE compared to WT, Sox21+/−, or to Sox2+/− CO exposed mice.
source: At 20 DPI, fewer FOXJ1+ ciliated cells, but more dividing and non-dividing basal cells were observed in Sox2+/− TE compared to WT, Sox21+/−, or to Sox2+/− CO exposed mice (Figure 5D–E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 5D-E and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Both WT and Sox21+/− TE had a similar number of ciliated cells, non-dividing basal cells, and dividing basal cells at 20 DPI compared to CO exposed mice.
source: Both WT and Sox21+/− TE had a similar number of ciliated cells, non-dividing basal cells, and dividing basal cells at 20 DPI compared to CO exposed mice (Figure 4D, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Recovery of injury in the WT and Sox21+/− TE appears the same, while Sox2+/− TE show a delayed recovery.
source: Thus, recovery of injury in the WT and Sox21+/− TE appears the same, while Sox2+/− TE show a delayed recovery (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), indicating an important role for SOX2 in TE regeneration.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the naphthalene injury data.

claim: SOX2 has an important role in TE regeneration.
source: Thus, recovery of injury in the WT and Sox21+/− TE appears the same, while Sox2+/− TE show a delayed recovery (Figure 5E, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D), indicating an important role for SOX2 in TE regeneration.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the naphthalene injury data.

claim: SOX21 is enriched in SOX2+ stalk (differentiating bronchiole) versus tip (distal) progenitor cells of the human fetal lung.
source: SOX21 is enriched in SOX2+ stalk (differentiating bronchiole) versus tip (distal) progenitor cells of the human fetal lung (Nikolić et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Sporadic SOX21-expressing cells were observed in lung sections at post-conceptional week (PCW) 17, mainly found in larger airways, where basal cells were also present.
source: We observed sporadic SOX21-expressing cells in lung sections at post-conceptional week (PCW) 17. The SOX21-expressing cells were mainly found in larger airways, where basal cells were also present (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6A.

claim: All cells within the human fetal lung tip organoids were positive for SOX2 and co-expressed either SOX9, SOX21, or both.
source: All cells within the organoids were positive for SOX2 and co-expressed either SOX9, SOX21, or both, unlike human PCW 17 lung sections (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Some SOX21-expressing cells in the fetal lung organoids were positive for the basal cell marker TP63, just like in human fetal lung sections.
source: Some SOX21-expressing cells in the fetal lung organoids were positive for the basal cell marker TP63, just like in human fetal lung sections (Figure 6A,B, white arrowheads).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Differentiation of human fetal lung tip organoids into airway organoids caused the lung organoids to take on a differentiated airway epithelium phenotype, with an increase in basal cells and the appearance of ciliated cells.
source: To induce maturation, we replaced fetal lung organoid medium with airway organoid medium as recently described (see Materials and Methods, Table 1; Sachs et al., 2019). This caused the lung organoids to take on a differentiated airway epithelium phenotype, with an increase in basal cells and the appearance of ciliated cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6C and a citation to the method.

claim: In differentiated airway organoids, SOX21 expression was observed in most cells.
source: In these airway organoids, SOX21 expression was observed in most cells (Figure 6C), and we confirmed expression of SOX21 in adult airway epithelial cells using human bronchial sections (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6C.

claim: SOX21 is expressed in adult human airway epithelial cells.
source: In these airway organoids, SOX21 expression was observed in most cells (Figure 6C), and we confirmed expression of SOX21 in adult airway epithelial cells using human bronchial sections (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6D.

claim: Both SOX2 and SOX21 are expressed throughout the human bronchial epithelium.
source: Both SOX2 and SOX21 are expressed throughout the bronchial epithelium (Figure 6D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6D.

claim: Prolonged culturing of human airway epithelial cells resulted in a significant increase of SOX2 and a slight increase of SOX21.
source: Prolonged culturing resulted in a significant increase of SOX2 and a slight increase of SOX21 (Figure 7A, Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by qPCR data in Figure 7A and Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Both SOX2 and SOX21 were higher expressed in the apical layer compared to the basal layer in human ALI cultures.
source: Both SOX2 and SOX21 were higher expressed in the apical layer compared to the basal layer (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by fluorescence intensity measurements in Figure 7B.

claim: Most TP63+ basal cells were low in SOX2 and SOX21 expression (88.3%).
source: Most TP63+ basal cells were low in SOX2 and SOX21 expression (88.3%) (Figure 7—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by fluorescence intensity measurements in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Ciliated cells were high in SOX2 expression, while SOX21 was highest in non-ciliated cells.
source: Comparing FOXJ1+ and FOXJ1− nuclei showed that ciliated cells were high in SOX2 expression, while SOX21 was highest in non-ciliated cells (Figure 7B, Figure 7—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by fluorescence intensity measurements in Figure 7B and Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Most ciliated cells were SOX2highSOX21low (75%).
source: Furthermore, the intensities of either SOX2 or SOX21 for ciliated (FOXJ1+), basal (TP63+), and FOXJ1− TP63− cells, showed that SOX21 was mainly high in double-negative cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by fluorescence intensity measurements in Figure 7—figure supplement 1D.

claim: SOX21 was mainly high in FOXJ1− TP63− double-negative cells.
source: Furthermore, the intensities of either SOX2 or SOX21 for ciliated (FOXJ1+), basal (TP63+), and FOXJ1− TP63− cells, showed that SOX21 was mainly high in double-negative cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by fluorescence intensity measurements in Figure 7C.

claim: FOXJ1− TP63− double-negative cells are intermediate cells transitioning from basal cells to a ciliated or secretory cell fate, the para-basal cell.
source: We think that these double-negative cells are intermediate cells transitioning from basal cells to a ciliated or sercretory cell fate, the para-basal cell.
evidence: This is an interpretation stated in the Results section based on the fluorescence intensity data and the observation of SOX21high cells in between basal and luminal layers.

claim: Sections of human airway epithelium show SOX21high cells in between the basal and luminal layer, which also express both basal cell marker KRT5 and luminal cell marker KRT8.
source: In accordance with this observation, sections of human airway epithelium show SOX21high cells in between the basal and luminal layer, which also express both basal cell marker KRT5 and luminal cell marker KRT8 (Figure 6D 1–3, arrows).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6D.

claim: Published single-cell RNA data on human primary bronchial epithelial ALI culture confirmed that high levels of SOX21 mRNA denote an intermediate cell type.
source: Comparison of our expression results to published single-cell RNA data on human primary bronchial epithelial ALI culture (Plasschaert et al., 2018) confirmed that high levels of SOX21 mRNA denote an intermediate cell type.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by comparison to published single-cell RNA sequencing data.

claim: High levels of SOX2 were observed both in the intermediate state and in differentiated ciliated cells in published single-cell RNA data.
source: Furthermore, in line with our observation, high levels of SOX2 were observed both in the intermediate state and in differentiated ciliated cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by comparison to published single-cell RNA sequencing data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1E.

claim: An overall increase of FOXJ1+ cells was observed upon knockdown of SOX2 or SOX21 in several independent donor ALI cultures.
source: We observed an overall increase of FOXJ1+ cells upon knockdown of SOX2 or SOX21 in several independent donor ALI cultures (Figure 7D).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 7D.

claim: Knockdown of SOX2 or SOX21 in the human airway cells favor a FOXJ1+ cell type.
source: Thus, knockdown of SOX2 or SOX21 in the human airway cells favor a FOXJ1+ cell type, partly resembling the mouse ALI experiments (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the knockdown experiments in human ALI cultures.

claim: Despite the increase in FOXJ1+ nuclei, there was no increase in fully differentiated ciliated cells as determined by the formation of TubulinIV+ cilia.
source: Despite the increase in FOXJ1+ nuclei, we did not observe an increase in fully differentiated ciliated cells as determined by the formation of TubulinIV+ cilia (Figure 7—figure supplement 1G).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1G.

claim: The increase in FOXJ1+ nuclei is seemingly combined with an impaired ability to differentiate into MUC5B+ goblet cells.
source: However, the increase in FOXJ1+ nuclei is seemingly combined with an impaired ability to differentiate into MUC5B+ goblet cells (Figure 7E).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Results section and supported by quantitative immunofluorescence data in Figure 7E.

claim: Both SOX2 and SOX21 suppress basal to ciliated cell differentiation in human airways.
source: In conclusion, our data suggest that both SOX2 and SOX21 suppress basal to ciliated cell differentiation, while both seem to positively affect goblet cell differentiation in the human airways.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the knockdown experiments in human ALI cultures.

claim: Both SOX2 and SOX21 seem to positively affect goblet cell differentiation in the human airways.
source: In conclusion, our data suggest that both SOX2 and SOX21 suppress basal to ciliated cell differentiation, while both seem to positively affect goblet cell differentiation in the human airways.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Results section based on the knockdown experiments in human ALI cultures.

claim: SOX2+SOX21+ cells in murine and human fetal lung organoids are progenitor cells in an environment destined for differentiation.
source: Based on our findings, we propose that (1) SOX2+SOX21+ cells in murine and human fetal lung organoids are progenitor cells in an environment destined for differentiation and (2) that SOX21 is important in balancing maintenance and differentiation of SOX2+ airway progenitor cells.
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the Discussion section based on the collective findings from the study.

claim: SOX21 is important in balancing maintenance and differentiation of SOX2+ airway progenitor cells.
source: Based on our findings, we propose that (1) SOX2+SOX21+ cells in murine and human fetal lung organoids are progenitor cells in an environment destined for differentiation and (2) that SOX21 is important in balancing maintenance and differentiation of SOX2+ airway progenitor cells.
evidence: This is a proposal stated in the Discussion section based on the collective findings from the study.

claim: The chromatin regions targeted by SOX2 are cell-type specific.
source: SOX2 is a key regulator in regulating proliferation and differentiation in many different stem cells populations; however; the chromatin regions targeted by SOX2 are cell-type specific.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: The regulation of stem cells by SOX2 is dependent on both its co-factors and expression levels.
source: The regulation of stem cells by SOX2 is dependent on both its co-factors and expression levels (Brafman et al., 2013; Hagey et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SOX2 requires a certain threshold level of expression to induce SOX21.
source: We suggest that SOX2 requires a certain threshold level of expression to induce SOX21.
evidence: This is a suggestion stated in the Discussion section based on the correlation between high SOX2 and SOX21 expression.

claim: SOX21 expression was first observed during the embryonic stage (E10.5–11.5), at a time when cells adopt a proximally restricted fate for the extrapulmonary airways.
source: Interestingly, SOX21 expression was first observed during the embryonic stage (E10.5–11.5), at a time when cells adopt a proximally restricted fate for the extrapulmonary airways (Yang et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and supported by the data from the study and a citation to previous literature.

claim: SOX21 is a downstream effector of SOX2 during formation of the extrapulmonary airways, separating extrapulmonary airway progenitors from intrapulmonary airway which are only SOX2 positive.
source: We suggest that SOX21 is a downstream effector of SOX2 during formation of the extrapulmonary airways, separating extrapulmonary airway progenitors from intrapulmonary airway which are only SOX2 positive.
evidence: This is a suggestion stated in the Discussion section based on the expression patterns and functional data.

claim: A similar induction of SOX21 by SOX2 has been described in the four-cell-stage embryo, in embryonic stem cells and in neuronal progenitor cells.
source: A similar induction of SOX21 by SOX2 has been described in the four-cell-stage embryo, in embryonic stem cells and in neuronal progenitor cells.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The function of SOX21 and its synergy or antagonism with SOX2 activity is highly context dependent.
source: The function of SOX21 and its synergy or antagonism with SOX2 activity is highly context dependent (Kopp et al., 2008; Mallanna et al., 2010; Chakravarthy et al., 2011; Goolam et al., 2016; Graham et al., 2003; Ohba et al., 2004; Sandberg et al., 2005; Matsuda et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Upon ectopic expression of SOX21, SOX9+ distal progenitor cells were maintained, with no differentiation to SOX2+ progenitor cells.
source: As an example of the context-dependent function of SOX21, we showed that upon ectopic expression of SOX21, SOX9+ distal progenitor cells were maintained, with no differentiation to SOX2+ progenitor cells.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and refers to data presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: SOX21 itself is not capable of driving differentiation to SOX2+ progenitor cells in the presence of distal mesenchymal signaling.
source: Thus, SOX21 itself is not capable of driving differentiation to SOX2+ progenitor cells in the presence of distal mesenchymal signaling.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section based on the transgenic mouse data.

claim: SOX2 and SOX21 can physically interact.
source: SOX2 and SOX21 can physically interact (Mallanna et al., 2010), and preliminary data of a genome-wide chromatin immunoprecipitation of the human airway ALI cultures showed that SOX2 and SOX21 not only have unique binding sites, but also co-occupy the same genomic regions (Figure 7—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation to previous literature and preliminary ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1H.

claim: SOX2 and SOX21 not only have unique binding sites, but also co-occupy the same genomic regions.
source: SOX2 and SOX21 can physically interact (Mallanna et al., 2010), and preliminary data of a genome-wide chromatin immunoprecipitation of the human airway ALI cultures showed that SOX2 and SOX21 not only have unique binding sites, but also co-occupy the same genomic regions (Figure 7—figure supplement 1H).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and supported by preliminary ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1H.

claim: The presence of SOX21 is important to suppress the differentiation of SOX2+ progenitor cells into basal and ciliated cells.
source: Using Sox21+/− and Sox21−/− mice, we showed that the presence of SOX21 is important to suppress the differentiation of SOX2+ progenitor cells into basal and ciliated cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section based on the data from Sox21+/− and Sox21−/− mice.

claim: The seemingly contradictory result of increased basal cells upon both deletion and overexpression of SOX21 may be caused by the difference in timing between the mouse models.
source: This seemingly contradictory result may be caused by the difference in timing between the mouse models.
evidence: This is an explanation stated in the Discussion section to reconcile the different phenotypes observed.

claim: The Sox21−/− mice lack Sox21 expression from the onset of lung development, which may trigger an expansion of basal cells.
source: The Sox21−/− mice lack expression of Sox21 from the fertilization of the oocyte, whereas the transgenic overexpressing mice only start to express SOX21 when the SPC or SCGB1A1 promoters become active. Thus, the Sox21−/− mice lack Sox21 expression from the onset of lung development, which may trigger an expansion of basal cells, whereas the overexpression of SOX21 is induced in differentiated epithelial cells.
evidence: This is an explanation stated in the Discussion section to reconcile the different phenotypes observed.

claim: The overexpression of SOX21 is induced in differentiated epithelial cells and may cause a reversal of differentiated cells to basal cells.
source: Thus, the Sox21−/− mice lack Sox21 expression from the onset of lung development, which may trigger an expansion of basal cells, whereas the overexpression of SOX21 is induced in differentiated epithelial cells. The SPC or SCGB1A1 promoter-driven expression of SOX21 may cause a reversal of differentiated cells to basal cells.
evidence: This is an explanation stated in the Discussion section to reconcile the different phenotypes observed.

claim: High levels of SOX21 may force cells to lose their identity followed by redifferentiation according to downstream cues received from the surrounding mesenchyme.
source: Alternatively, high levels of SOX21 may force cells to lose their identity followed by redifferentiation according to downstream cues received from the surrounding mesenchyme.
evidence: This is an alternative explanation stated in the Discussion section.

claim: SPC-promoter-driven induction of SOX21 initiates the reversal of SOX9+ cells to a proximal phenotype, but this only becomes apparent once these SOX9+ cells are sufficiently distanced from distal mesenchymal FGF10 signaling.
source: For example, SPC-promoter-driven induction of SOX21 initiates the reversal of SOX9+ cells to a proximal phenotype, but this only becomes apparent once these SOX9+ cells are sufficiently distanced from distal mesenchymal FGF10 signaling.
evidence: This is an explanation stated in the Discussion section based on the transgenic mouse data.

claim: The initiation of a proximal cell fate by ectopic expression of SOX21, followed by SOX2 expression, may explain why the cysts in SOX21-expressing lungs are smaller than the cysts observed upon ectopic expression of SOX2.
source: The initiation of a proximal cell fate by ectopic expression of SOX21, followed by SOX2 expression, may explain why the cysts in SOX21-expressing lungs are smaller than the cysts observed upon ectopic expression of SOX2, the major proximal cell fate inducer.
evidence: This is an explanation stated in the Discussion section based on the transgenic mouse data.

claim: SOX21 and SOX2 co-expression continues in adult TE and SMGs, which are both regions where progenitor cells reside.
source: SOX21 and SOX2 co-expression continues in adult TE and SMGs, which are both regions where progenitor cells reside.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and supported by the immunofluorescence data presented earlier.

claim: Reduced SOX2 levels inhibit the contribution of SOX9+ SMG cells to repair of TE injury, while reduced SOX21 levels promote their contribution.
source: We showed that reduced SOX2 levels inhibit the contribution of SOX9+ SMG cells to repair of TE injury, while reduced SOX21 levels promote their contribution.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section based on the naphthalene injury data.

claim: Reduced SOX2 levels decreased differentiation of basal to ciliated cells in vitro and in vivo.
source: Furthermore, reduced SOX2 levels decreased differentiation of basal to ciliated cells in vitro and in vivo, while reduced SOX21 levels only increased basal cell differentiation in vitro but not in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section based on the ALI culture and naphthalene injury data.

claim: Reduced SOX21 levels only increased basal cell differentiation in vitro but not in vivo.
source: Furthermore, reduced SOX2 levels decreased differentiation of basal to ciliated cells in vitro and in vivo, while reduced SOX21 levels only increased basal cell differentiation in vitro but not in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section based on the ALI culture and naphthalene injury data.

claim: Differentiation of progenitor cells in vivo is regulated by an epithelial–mesenchymal interaction, which might inhibit further differentiation to ciliated cells when regeneration is complete.
source: The latter might be explained by the fact that differentiation of progenitor cells in vivo is regulated by an epithelial–mesenchymal interaction, which might inhibit further differentiation to ciliated cells when regeneration is complete (Volckaert et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an explanation stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: Both during development and regeneration of the airway epithelium, endogenous SOX21 acts as a suppressor of SOX2+ progenitor cell differentiation, while SOX2 levels are important for stimulating differentiation.
source: In summary, both during development and regeneration of the airway epithelium, endogenous SOX21 acts as a suppressor of SOX2+ progenitor cell differentiation, while SOX2 levels are important for stimulating differentiation.
evidence: This is a summary statement in the Discussion section based on the collective data from the study.

claim: SOX21 can antagonize SOX2 function on certain promotor regions.
source: Using a luciferase assay, we specifically show that SOX21 can antagonize SOX2 function on certain promotor regions.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and supported by the luciferase assay data presented earlier.

claim: To fully understand the function of SOX21 within SOX2+ airway progenitors, signaling/environmental cues, additional co-factors, and expression levels are likely to play a role.
source: However, to fully understand the function of SOX21 within SOX2+ airway progenitors, signaling/environmental cues, additional co-factors, and expression levels are likely to play a role.
evidence: This is a statement in the Discussion section acknowledging the complexity of the regulatory mechanisms.

claim: SOX2 and SOX21 showed a similar but not identical expression pattern in human airway epithelium.
source: SOX2 and SOX21 showed a similar but not identical expression pattern in human airway epithelium.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and supported by the immunofluorescence data from human samples.

claim: The human proximal airway epithelium contains an additional layer of intermediate cells or para-basal cells compared to mouse tracheal epithelium.
source: As opposed to mouse tracheal epithelium which has a basal and luminal cell layer, the human proximal airway epithelium contains an additional layer of intermediate cells or para-basal cells (Mercer et al., 1994; Boers et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: High SOX21 levels in TP63− FOXJ1− cells represent the intermediate layer of para-basal cells transitioning to a luminal cell fate.
source: Using human primary bronchial epithelial ALI cultures, we showed high SOX21 levels in TP63− FOXJ1− cells and suggest that these cells represent the intermediate layer of para-basal cells transitioning to a luminal cell fate.
evidence: This is a suggestion stated in the Discussion section based on the fluorescence intensity data from human ALI cultures.

claim: In mouse ALI cultures, reduced SOX2 expression resulted in a decrease in ciliated cells, whereas reduced SOX21 expression resulted in an increase in ciliated cells without affecting secretory cell numbers.
source: In mouse ALI cultures, reduced SOX2 expression resulted in a decrease in ciliated cells, whereas reduced SOX21 expression resulted in an increase in ciliated cells without affecting secretory cell numbers.
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and refers to data presented earlier in the manuscript.

claim: Human basal cells comprise at least four basal cell types, whereas mice only have one basal cell population.
source: Recently, human basal cells were shown to comprise at least four basal cell types, whereas mice only have one basal cell population (Travaglini et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is stated in the Discussion section and supported by a citation to recent literature.

claim: De-regulation of SOX2 and SOX21 expression levels can alter branching morphogenesis and differentiation of airway epithelium.
source: Our data provide a new understanding of proximal–distal patterning of the airways and the regulation of SOX2 progenitor cells within development and regeneration of airway epithelium. De-regulation of SOX2 and SOX21 expression levels can alter branching morphogenesis and differentiation of airway epithelium.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the Discussion section based on the collective data from the study.

claim: SOX21 can act as a suppressor of differentiation when SOX2 expression levels are high and when progenitor cells are prone to differentiate.
source: We show that SOX21 can act as a suppressor of differentiation when SOX2 expression levels are high and when progenitor cells are prone to differentiate.
